problems.title: A known-label bridge is substituted for a marginal reverse law
claim: Eq. (\(6\)) treats the known-\(y_0\) reverse bridge as the marginal reverse law conditioned only on \(y_t,x\).
analysis: The marginal is a mixture over \(q(y_0\mid y_t,x)\). If bridge means are \(a_ty_0+b_ty_t\) and common bridge covariance is \(\widetilde\beta_tI\), total covariance gives \(\operatorname{Cov}(y_{t-1}\mid y_t,x)=\widetilde\beta_tI+a_t^2\operatorname{Cov}(y_0\mid y_t,x)\). A two-point label posterior with nonzero weights has positive extra covariance whenever the bridge coefficient is nonzero. Deleting \(y_0\) from conditioning cannot delete that term, even with arbitrarily small positive forward noise. The proposed universal decoder-gradient necessity does not follow.
result: The claimed exact reverse-law derivation omits posterior-label mixture covariance, undermining the asserted universal decoder-gradient necessity. A Gaussian reverse approximation can still be a useful model.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Use the actual mixture or conditional-moment law and justify any Gaussian approximation separately.
problems.impact_rationale: The core reverse-distribution derivation substitutes a conditional bridge for a mixture and drops a positive total-covariance term. The decoder-necessity argument is therefore unsupported by its claimed identity.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Co-occurrence weights depend on class numbering
problems.source_location: utils/knn_utils.py and all three training call sites.
claim: The co-occurrence weighting is intended to depend on label relationships rather than arbitrary class IDs.
analysis: The author's class-pair weight function changes sample weights under a simultaneous permutation of label coordinates and co-occurrence rows/columns. Thus arbitrary label numbering can alter the training objective. A symmetric unordered-pair rule can restore numbering invariance, but neither its optimality nor corrected benchmark performance is established.

For a realizable co-occurrence count matrix with pair counts \(c_{01}=1,c_{02}=3,c_{12}=1\), row normalization gives upper-pair scores \((1/4,3/4,1/2)\). A batch containing those three label pairs receives approximately \((1/2,1,3/4)\) after the released min–max scaling. Simultaneously swapping class IDs \(0,1\) and the matrix axes changes the pair scores to \((1/2,3/4,1/2)\), and scaled weights to approximately \((1/2,1,1/2)\). The lower-ID directional lookup changes a sample weight despite unchanged label relations.
result: The released weighting rule is not invariant under arbitrary relabeling of class IDs. No corrected benchmark performance is inferred.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Specify and use a permutation-invariant class-pair statistic with an explicit normalization.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The active target is a vector rather than the described matrix
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, p.5; Algorithm 1, p.7; train_on_Voc2007.py:96–118; utils/model_diffusion.py.
claim: The paper and Algorithm1 specify a \(C\)-by-\(C\) one-hot diffusion target.
analysis: The release passes batch-by-\(C\) neighborhood vectors to forward_t, and the network returns \(C\) outputs. There is no active conversion to the claimed \(C\times C\) target; an unused one-hot helper does not implement it. Vector diffusion can be valid, but it has a different representation rationale.
result: The released vector target is a different representation from the stated matrix target.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Document vector diffusion explicitly or supply the actual matrix encoding/decoding path and rerun matched comparisons.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The depicted trainable encoder is outside the optimizer
problems.source_location: Figure B.1, p.25; optimizer construction and training/evaluation mode calls.
claim: Figure B.1 marks the diffusion feature encoder trainable, distinct from the intentionally frozen fp_encoder.
analysis: The optimizer includes the noise head but omits diffusion_encoder. Backward can create encoder gradients without updating its parameters; optimizer.zero_grad also does not clear excluded gradients. Evaluation sets that separate encoder to eval and the next model.train does not restore it. This does not mean every buffer was frozen from the first step.
result: The optimizer does not update the separately declared trainable diffusion encoder, and its mode is not restored as stated.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: If trainable as specified, include diffusion_encoder parameters and restore its train mode; preserve the separately intended frozen fp_encoder.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Checkpoint selection uses test mAP
problems.source_location: Three training entries, best-mAP checkpoint condition and dataset loaders.
claim: The paper describes a validation-based model-selection protocol.
analysis: The release evaluates the held-out test loader each epoch and uses its mAP to update the best checkpoint. This makes those source-path test results part of selection. It does not prove every published experiment used the default snapshot.
result: The public checkpoint selector uses held-out test mAP, differing from a validation-only protocol.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Create disjoint training/validation/test identities and select on validation only; the complete paper scores were not recomputed.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Classwise zero-count guards contaminate overall F1
claim: The release names its aggregate metric overall F1.
analysis: The metric replaces zero per-class prediction/ground-truth counts by one before global summation. With true positives \((1,0)\), predicted-positive counts \((1,0)\), and actual-positive counts \((1,1)\), correct overall F1 is \(2/3\). The fabricated second predicted positive changes it to \(1/2\). Division guards must not change raw global counts.
result: The routine alters raw global counts before computing overall F1 and fails the two-class control.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Keep original counts for global precision/recall and use masked division only for classwise summaries.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: COCO noise and validation options are not implemented by the default path
problems.source_location: train_on_COCO.py and utils/data_coco.py; paper dataset/protocol section.
claim: The entry exposes noise-type and validation-split options.
analysis: The COCO constructor call does not forward the requested noise_type, and the split_per parameter is not used to create the declared validation partition. Passing a different CLI value therefore does not establish a different noise law or a real validation split on that path. External preprocessing could explain historical runs, but is unrecorded.
result: The COCO entry does not implement the exposed noise/split settings on the checked path. Historical external preprocessing is unresolved.
assumptions: The exact source version and operative conditions stated in this analysis.
repair: Forward the requested noise type and implement an actual disjoint validation split with identifiable samples.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
